units.leftText: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ for the faith of God’s elect and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,
units.rightText: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s elect, and the knowledge of the truth which is according to godliness,

units.leftText: in the hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before time began.
units.rightText: in hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before times eternal;

units.leftText: In His own time He has made His word evident in the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior.
units.rightText: but in his own seasons manifested his word in the message, wherewith I was intrusted according to the commandment of God our Saviour;

units.leftText: To Titus, my true child in our common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior. Appointing Elders on Crete (1 Timothy 3:1–7|1TI 3:1-7*; 1 Peter 5:1–4|1PE 5:1-4*)
units.rightText: to Titus, my true child after a common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Saviour.

units.leftText: The reason I left you in Crete was that you would set in order what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
units.rightText: For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that were wanting, and appoint elders in every city, as I gave thee charge;

units.leftText: An elder must be blameless, the husband of but one wife, having children who are believers and who are not open to accusation of indiscretion or insubordination.
units.rightText: if any man is blameless, the husband of one wife, having children that believe, who are not accused of riot or unruly.

units.leftText: As God’s steward, an overseer must be above reproach — not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to drunkenness, not violent, not greedy for money.
units.rightText: For the bishop must be blameless, as God’s steward; not self-willed, not soon angry, no brawler, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre;

units.leftText: Instead, he must be hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined.
units.rightText: but given to hospitality, a lover of good, sober-minded, just, holy, self-controlled;

units.leftText: He must hold firmly to the faithful word as it was taught, so that he can encourage others by sound teaching and refute those who contradict it. Correcting False Teachers (1 Timothy 1:3–11|1TI 1:3-11*)
units.rightText: holding to the faithful word which is according to the teaching, that he may be able both to exhort in the sound doctrine, and to convict the gainsayers.

units.leftText: For many are rebellious and full of empty talk and deception, especially those of the circumcision,
units.rightText: For there are many unruly men, vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision,

units.leftText: who must be silenced. For the sake of dishonorable gain, they undermine entire households and teach things they should not.
units.rightText: whose mouths must be stopped; men who overthrow whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre’s sake.

units.leftText: As one of their own prophets has said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.”
units.rightText: One of themselves, a prophet of their own, said, Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, idle gluttons.
leftNotes: 1:12 This quote, also known as the Epimenides paradox, has been attributed to the Cretan philosopher Epimenides of Knossos.

units.leftText: This testimony is true. Therefore rebuke them sternly, so that they will be sound in the faith
units.rightText: This testimony is true. For which cause reprove them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,

units.leftText: and will pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of men who have rejected the truth.
units.rightText: not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men who turn away from the truth.

units.leftText: To the pure, all things are pure; but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Indeed, both their minds and their consciences are defiled.
units.rightText: To the pure all things are pure: but to them that are defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure; but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.

units.leftText: They profess to know God, but by their actions they deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good deed.
units.rightText: They profess that they know God; but by their works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.

units.leftText: But as for you, speak the things that are consistent with sound doctrine.
units.rightText: But speak thou the things which befit the sound doctrine:

units.leftText: Older men are to be temperate, dignified, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and perseverance.
units.rightText: that aged men be temperate, grave, sober-minded, sound in faith, in love, in patience:

units.leftText: Older women, likewise, are to be reverent in their behavior, not slanderers or addicted to much wine, but teachers of good.
units.rightText: that aged women likewise be reverent in demeanor, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of that which is good;

units.leftText: In this way they can train the young women to love their husbands and children,
units.rightText: that they may train the young women to love their husbands, to love their children,

units.leftText: to be self-controlled, pure, managers of their households, kind, and submissive to their own husbands, so that the word of God will not be discredited.
units.rightText: to be sober-minded, chaste, workers at home, kind, being in subjection to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed:

units.leftText: In the same way, urge the younger men to be self-controlled.
units.rightText: the younger men likewise exhort to be sober-minded:

units.leftText: In everything, show yourself to be an example by doing good works. In your teaching show integrity, dignity,
units.rightText: in all things showing thyself an ensample of good works; in thy doctrine showing uncorruptness, gravity,

units.leftText: and wholesome speech that is above reproach, so that anyone who opposes us will be ashamed, having nothing bad to say about us.
units.rightText: sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of us.

units.leftText: Slaves are to submit to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not argumentative,
units.rightText: Exhort servants to be in subjection to their own masters, and to be well-pleasing to them in all things; not gainsaying;

units.leftText: not stealing from them, but showing all good faith, so that in every respect they will adorn the teaching about God our Savior. God’s Grace Brings Salvation
units.rightText: not purloining, but showing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.

units.leftText: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone.
units.rightText: For the grace of God hath appeared, bringing salvation to all men,

units.leftText: It instructs us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live sensible, upright, and godly lives in the present age,
units.rightText: instructing us, to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly and righteously and godly in this present world;

units.leftText: as we await the blessed hope and glorious appearance of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;

units.leftText: He gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people for His own possession, zealous for good deeds.
units.rightText: who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a people for his own possession, zealous of good works.

units.leftText: Speak these things as you encourage and rebuke with all authority. Let no one despise you.
units.rightText: These things speak and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no man despise thee.

units.leftText: Remind the believers to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient and ready for every good work,
units.rightText: Put them in mind to be in subjection to rulers, to authorities, to be obedient, to be ready unto every good work,

units.leftText: to malign no one, and to be peaceable and gentle, showing full consideration to everyone.
units.rightText: to speak evil of no man, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all meekness toward all men.

units.leftText: For at one time we too were foolish, disobedient, misled, and enslaved to all sorts of desires and pleasures — living in malice and envy, being hated and hating one another.
units.rightText: For we also once were foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, hating one another.

units.leftText: But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for mankind appeared,
units.rightText: But when the kindness of God our Saviour, and his love toward man, appeared,

units.leftText: He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy, through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: not by works done in righteousness, which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy he saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit,

units.leftText: This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
units.rightText: which he poured out upon us richly, through Jesus Christ our Saviour;

units.leftText: so that, having been justified by His grace, we would become heirs with the hope of eternal life.
units.rightText: that, being justified by his grace, we might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

units.leftText: This saying is trustworthy. And I want you to emphasize these things, so that those who have believed God will take care to devote themselves to good deeds. These things are excellent and profitable for the people. Avoid Divisions (Romans 16:17–20|ROM 16:17-20*)
units.rightText: Faithful is the saying, and concerning these things I desire that thou affirm confidently, to the end that they who have believed God may be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men:

units.leftText: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, arguments, and quarrels about the law, because these things are pointless and worthless.
units.rightText: but shun foolish questionings, and genealogies, and strifes, and fightings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.

units.leftText: Reject a divisive man after a first and second admonition,
units.rightText: A factious man after a first and second admonition refuse;

units.leftText: knowing that such a man is corrupt and sinful; he is self-condemned. Final Remarks and Greetings
units.rightText: knowing that such a one is perverted, and sinneth, being self-condemned.

units.leftText: As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to winter there.
units.rightText: When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, give diligence to come unto me to Nicopolis: for there I have determined to winter.

units.leftText: Do your best to equip Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that they will have everything they need.
units.rightText: Set forward Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them.

units.leftText: And our people must also learn to devote themselves to good works in order to meet the pressing needs of others, so that they will not be unfruitful.
units.rightText: And let our people also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.

units.leftText: All who are with me send you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with all of you.
units.rightText: All that are with me salute thee. Salute them that love us in faith. Grace be with you all.
